newsitem.title: USA: US July spot natgas off 10-15 cts from June index.
newsitem.headline: US July spot natgas off 10-15 cts from June index.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for July 1 fell about 10-15 cents from June indices Friday as ample storage supplies and the upcoming holiday weekend kept buyers cautious, market sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices for July 1 were quoted at $2.15-2.18 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub, still about two cents under weekend values and off about 15 cents from June indices.

U.S. gas stocks are about 19 percent ahead of year-ago tallies, with the Producing Region leading the pack at plus 54 percent. The West Region, which had been dangerously low, was just about 10 percent shy of year-ago levels, according to AGA.
In the East, where stocks gained 65 bcf last week to 19 percent above a year ago, New York city gate prices for July 1 were quoted in the mid-$2.40s.
For weekend delivery, prices at the city-gate softened into the mid-to-high $2.40s though temperature highs in the region were forecast to hover near 90 degrees F through early next week.
In the Midwest, July 1 prices were quoted mostly around $2, off almost 15 cents from June indices. For the weekend, prices also softened to about $2.
Chicago city-gate for next month was talked in the low-to-mid $2.20s.
In West Texas, Permian prices for July 1 were quoted at $1.96-1.98, down about 10 cents from Thursday. Weekend values were talked in the high-$1.80s to mid-$1.90s.
At the southern California border, July 1 gas traded mostly at $2.14 and $2.15.
San Juan prices dove into the mid-$1.70s to low-$1.80s for the weekend and low-$1.90s for July 1, traders said.
